sequence.body:
Welcome to Combat Patrol! Whether you are a new recruit to Warhammer 40,000 or a seasoned veteran, Combat Patrol is all about getting your forces into action as quickly as possible.

Combat Patrol is the quickest and simplest way to start collecting and playing Warhammer 40,000. In Combat Patrol battles, each player will command a compact army of Warhammer miniatures in tactical clashes that should last up to one hour.

Typically comprising the contents of a Combat Patrol box, every Combat Patrol force is a great starting point for any aspiring Warhammer 40,000 general. As well as being amazing tools for collecting, the models from each one can face off against each other in quick and exciting pickup games. There is no need to create an army list and add up points values; simply choose your favourite faction, assemble your miniatures and prepare for war.

Combat Patrol games are fast-paced and action-packed; victory is determined primarily through expert tactical play, but a healthy dose of good luck never hurts! Each Combat Patrol will have a set mission that it is trying to complete, rewarding its player with crucial Victory points. At the battle’s end, when the smoke has cleared, victory will go to the player who has scored the most of these.

As well as being the best way to play quick games of Warhammer 40,000, Combat Patrol is a great opportunity to try out different factions and familiarise yourself with the unique tactics and play styles of each one. Whichever you choose, you will soon learn your army’s strengths and weaknesses and gain the skills needed to claim victories on larger battlefields.
sequence.title: Combat Patrol Mission Sequence

sequence.body: Each player selects one Combat Patrol to use.
sequence.title: Select Combat Patrols

sequence.body:
Roll one D6 and consult the table below to determine one of the deployment maps. This describes where to place **terrain features**, **objectives** and where you can deploy your armies.

◈ D6 | Deployment Map
◈ 1–2 | Layout A
◈ 3–4 | Layout B
◈ 5–6 | Layout C
sequence.title: Determine Deployment

sequence.body:
Missions are played on rectangular battlefields 44” by 30” in size.

Players should set up the **terrain features** as shown in the deployment map.
sequence.title: Create the Battlefield

sequence.body:
Players look at the deployment map and agree which edges of your battlefield correspond with the Attacker’s and Defender’s battlefield edges labelled on the map.

Roll off: the winner decides who will be the Attacker and who will be the Defender.
sequence.title: Determine Attacker and Defender

sequence.body:
Players secretly note down:
▪ Which of their units will start the battle embarked within which **Transports**.
▪ Which of their units will start the battle in **strategic reserves**. The combined number of such units cannot exceed more than half the number of units in that player’s Combat Patrol.
▪ Which of their **leader** units will start the battle attached to which **bodyguard** units (this is optional).
▪ Which one of their two available **enhancements** they will use.

Players then reveal these decisions. Each player's **Warlord** model is specified in their Combat Patrol. These models have the WARLORD keyword.

Some Combat Patrols require certain units to be set up in **strategic reserves**, these still count towards the limit of how many units from a player’s army can be in **strategic reserves**.
sequence.title: Declare Battle Formations

sequence.body: Players take it in turns to set up their units (excluding those in **strategic reserves**) one at a time, wholly within their deployment zone, starting with the Defender. Once you have finished setting up your units, if your opponent has any units that have not been set up, they set up those units.
sequence.title: Deploy Armies

sequence.body: Roll off: the winner takes the first turn.
sequence.title: Determine First Turn

sequence.body: Players alternate resolving any pre-battle rules units from their army may have, starting with the player who will take the first turn.
sequence.title: Resolve Pre-Battle Rules

sequence.body:
The first battle round begins. Each player should look at their Combat Patrol’s mission to see what they need to do in order to score Victory Points.

**Stratagems**

Combat Patrol games reflect a battle between two small forces of troops. As such they lack access to some of the logistical support found in larger armies. When playing a Combat Patrol game, the following **core stratagems** cannot be used:
▪ **Crushing Impact**
▪ **Explosives**
▪ **Rapid Ingress**
sequence.title: Begin The Battle

sequence.body: The battle ends after five battle rounds have been completed. Even if you have no models remaining in your army at the start of your turn, players continue to play out their turns until the battle ends.
sequence.title: End the Battle

sequence.body:
At the end of the battle, the player with the most VP is the victor. If the players are tied, the battle is a draw. Players will score VP from the following:
▪ Each player’s own Combat Patrol mission.
▪ Each player scores an additional 10VP if their army is painted to a Battle Ready standard.

If a player is new to the game and this is one of their first opportunities to get their Combat Patrol to the table, we recommend ignoring the 10VP awarded for painting to a Battle Ready standard. Though this should be applied at any Combat Patrol events.
sequence.title: Determine Victor
